page: Vultr voc-c-16c-32gb-300s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor with x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided by a bundled 300 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this server.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25% of tested servers. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests, such as read-only large block and write large block operations, also demonstrate average performance. Notably, the server achieves top-tier performance in text generation for small LLM models and strong performance for medium LLM models, while text processing benchmarks are also in the top 25%.

With dedicated CPU allocation and a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server offers a balanced compute-to-memory profile suitable for compute-bound workloads. The inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage enhances data retrieval speeds without requiring external storage attachments. This configuration is well-suited for workloads such as software compilation, text processing, web serving, and small-to-medium language model inference tasks that benefit from dedicated AMD EPYC processing cores.
